about: Published laws of genome evolution, re-tested on this project's data (scripts/run_literature.py). Statements paraphrase the cited papers.

laws.statement: Genes with low dispensability and high conservation have a low propensity to be lost (propensity for gene loss, PGL).
laws.source: Krylov, Wolf, Rogozin & Koonin 2003, Genome Research 13:2229
laws.our_test: Family loss rate in 79 parasite pairs vs ubiquity in free-living eukaryotes: Spearman -0.58 over 8416 families; least-ubiquitous quartile loses 68%, most-ubiquitous 24%.

laws.statement: Mitochondrial gene loss follows the same order across eukaryote lineages.
laws.our_test: Loss is strongly nested in mitochondria (containment 0.95 vs 0.78 random), explained by per-gene loss rates (fixed-fixed null 0.95).

laws.statement: The same gene features (hydrophobicity, pKa, GC) predict retention in mitochondria and plastids; a model trained on one predicts the other.
laws.our_test: Retention-rate model trained on mitochondria ranks plastid genes with Spearman 0.43 (plastid-trained, leave-one-gene-out: 0.50); plastid->mitochondria 0.36 (within 0.55). A shared component transfers, and system-specific laws fit better (endosymbiosis_v1, delta AIC 787).

laws.statement: Hydrophobic, membrane-embedded proteins are retained in organelle genomes because they are hard to import.
laws.our_test: Mitochondria: hydrophobicity loss weight -0.32 and TM helices -0.37 (both retained, CIs exclude 0). Plastids: no effect (CIs include 0). Insect endosymbionts, which import nothing: membrane proteins are lost more (+0.16).

laws.statement: In plants turning parasitic the plastome degrades in stages: ndh, then photosynthesis and plastid RNA polymerase, then ATP synthase, then housekeeping genes.
laws.source: Wicke & Naumann 2018; Graham et al. 2017, New Phytologist
laws.our_test: Epifagus vs tobacco: ndh 100%, photosynthesis+PEP 100%, ATP synthase 100%, housekeeping 23% lost. Monotone with stage. One lineage only; the plastid co-loss modules (organelle_modules_v1) also put ndh genes in one block.

laws.statement: Genes per functional category scale as a power of total gene number: transcription regulators and signalling ~N^2, metabolism ~N^1, translation ~N^0.
laws.our_test: Across 36 bacteria and archaea: transcription regulation exponent 1.95 [1.63, 2.27], signalling 2.47 [1.80, 3.36], metabolism 0.70 [0.53, 0.89], translation 0.01 [-0.02, 0.04].

laws.statement: Free-living bacteria lose 'leaky' functions that the community supplies, e.g. hydrogen-peroxide removal in Prochlorococcus.
laws.our_test: Synechococcus elongatus 2 catalase/peroxidase genes -> Prochlorococcus marinus 0; Cereibacter sphaeroides 3 catalase/peroxidase genes -> Candidatus Pelagibacter ubique 0.

laws.statement: Oligotrophs evolve small genomes with few regulators (selection for nutrient economy).
laws.our_test: Median genes 1598 (oligotrophs) vs 3327 (others); transcription regulators per 1000 genes 20 vs 60. Oligotrophy is the only environment axis that raises the share of families lost (severity_environment_v1, +0.80).

laws.statement: Bacterial genomes shrink through a pervasive bias toward deletions; in symbionts relaxed selection plus drift removes unused genes.
laws.source: Mira, Ochman & Moran 2001, Trends in Genetics 17:589
laws.our_test: Not testable with gene-family presence (needs indel spectra). Consistent in outline: insect endosymbionts lose ~85% of their ancestor's genes (severity_endosymbiosis_v1).
